data.reasoning: The package is a standard AUR wrapper for a prebuilt Electron application. The PKGBUILD downloads .deb archives from the official upstream CDN with pinned b2sum checksums, preventing supply-chain tampering. The wrapper script and desktop entry are benign. The only discrepancy between the reports is an API error in the qwen model for z-code.desktop, which deepseek successfully audited and cleared.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model encountered an HTTP 400 API error when auditing z-code.desktop, forcing an 'inconclusive' overall verdict. The deepseek model audited the same file without issue and correctly identified it as a safe, standard desktop entry.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit z-code.desktop due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400)
learnings: Transient API errors on individual files should not permanently block a safe verdict if the file is low-risk (like a .desktop file) or if another model in the ensemble successfully audits it.
Implement retry logic for individual file audits when encountering HTTP 400/500 errors before marking the entire package as inconclusive.
